title: Vilna Rising
premise: In the occupied city of Vilna, Orsen Ashgrove works as a battlefield nurse by day and secretly records the names of the dead that officers refuse to acknowledge in a hidden ledger. When a census taker named Ilse begins asking pointed questions about Orsen's missing papers and ambiguous identity, Orsen realizes the ledger itself could condemn everyone connected to it. Racing to complete the record of names before the spring thaw opens the river to troop transports—and before the workshop where the ledger is hidden is seized—Orsen must choose between erasing their own history to survive or claiming it at last. The book ends with Orsen entrusting the finished ledger to Ilse, who has become an unlikely ally, as the ice breaks and the workshop burns behind them.
about_author: A. M. Vasquez is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging displaced-persons records from Eastern Europe. They write historical fiction about the people history forgot to name.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. We meet Orsen in the surgical ward of Vilna's garrison hospital, stitching wounds by lamplight and secretly recording the names of dying soldiers the officers log only as numbers. The emotional beat is quiet defiance: Orsen believes names are a form of inheritance no occupation can confiscate.

chapters.title: A Question of Residence
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Census taker Ilse Brandt arrives at the boarding house with her forms and her unnervingly patient questions. She notices Orsen's papers list no birthplace. Orsen deflects, but the encounter leaves them shaken—the ledger hidden in the bookbinder's workshop downstairs suddenly feels heavier.

chapters.title: What the Officers Omit
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with a brief interlude from Ilse's field notes. A mass casualty day floods the ward; Orsen learns three men died unnamed because their units disowned them as deserters. Grief hardens into resolve: the ledger must be finished before the river ice breaks and the garrison relocates.

chapters.title: The Bookbinder's Daughter
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Flashbacks interleave with the present as Orsen visits the workshop of Marta, the old bookbinder sheltering them, and we learn Orsen's true parentage—a father erased from every record for political reasons. Identity emerges as both wound and inheritance; Orsen fears claiming it will doom Marta too.

chapters.title: Ilse Returns
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Orsen and Ilse. Ilse comes back with follow-up questions but also contraband coffee and an apology she doesn't explain. Their charged conversation reveals Ilse is herself keeping secrets—her brother was one of the numbered dead. The beat is wary attraction blooming across an impossible divide.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. An officer orders the workshop inventoried for requisition. Orsen and Marta hide the ledger inside a false binding of a hymnal while soldiers measure the shelves. The tension is claustrophobic; Orsen realizes the ice on the river is groaning earlier than any year in memory.

chapters.title: Names in the Ice
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse discovers the ledger by accident while cross-checking census entries against hospital rolls. Instead of reporting it, she adds her brother's name in her own hand. Her chapter is the moral pivot: duty and love stop being opposites, and she becomes complicit in Orsen's work.

chapters.title: The Last Blank Page
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. With the thaw imminent, Orsen works through the night completing the final pages, racing a requisition order signed for dawn. Marta is detained at a checkpoint; Orsen must decide whether to flee alone or stay to finish. The emotional beat is sacrifice sharpened into clarity—finishing the work is finishing themselves.

chapters.title: When the River Breaks
chapters.summary: Orsen and Ilse, alternating. The ice cracks open as troops pour toward the bridges. Ilse falsifies Orsen's transit papers using her census authority, and together they carry the ledger out as the workshop is set alight for 'sanitation.' The climax fuses love, duty, and identity into a single act of witness amid chaos.

chapters.title: Everything That Remains Is Given
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, epilogue-like. On a crowded barge heading downstream, Orsen gives the completed ledger to a courier bound for neutral territory, keeping only one page—the page bearing their own father's restored name. Free at last of secrecy, Orsen takes Ilse's hand. The resolution is quiet joy: inheritance is not what we hide, but what we pass on.
